scenes.headline: How Bonsai 2 packs a 27B model into ternary
scenes.sub: Trits, group scales, and a Hadamard rotation the runtime has to apply.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Sequoia! Bonsai 2 stores a twenty-seven-billion-parameter model as ternary weights in about six gigabytes. Here's how the format works.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Each weight is minus one, zero or plus one, times a shared scale, stored in a rotated basis that the runtime must match on every pass.

scenes.title: Ternary rides a 2-bit matmul
scenes.say: Here's the neat trick in the format.

parts.note: stored as an unsigned 2-bit code: 0, 1 or 2
parts.say: Each trit is stored as an unsigned code: zero, one or two.
Subtract one, and you're back at minus one, zero, plus one.
Times one sixteen-bit scale per hundred and twenty-eight weights. So ternary rides a stock affine two-bit matmul.

scenes.title: Two packings of the same trits

left.title: PQ2_0: a slot per trit
left.say: One packing gives every trit its own two-bit slot: thirty-four bytes per block, cheaper to decode.

right.title: PTQ1_0: dense trits
right.say: The other packs trits densely: twenty-eight bytes, five point nine five gigabytes, but unpacking costs arithmetic. Which wins depends on the GPU.

scenes.title: What the runtime does, per projection

steps.note: a fixed Walsh-Hadamard rotation per 1024-weight block
steps.say: Before ternarizing, each block of one thousand and twenty-four weights was rotated by a fixed transform.
So on every forward pass, the runtime flips signs and applies the same rotation to the activations.
Then a two-bit matmul unpacks the trits and applies the scales. Stock llama.cpp rejects these formats, which is why PrismML ships its own kernels.

scenes.title: Kept from full precision
scenes.say: The headline keeps ninety-eight point two percent on average. On the two long-horizon agentic benchmarks, it keeps about three-quarters.

scenes.text: Ternary is a memory win, not automatically a compute win: it needs kernels and a runtime built for it.

recap: Trits as 2-bit codes, times an FP16 scale
98.2% on average, about 75% on agentic runs
scenes.say: To recap: codes times a scale, a rotation the runtime must match, and retention that depends on the workload.
